findings.title: /api/v1/companion/today turns a database refusal into an untyped HTTP 500
findings.request: GET /api/v1/companion/today?businessId=<zemnas>&userId=<admin id> with osama@nexus.local (standard user, zemnas access)
findings.response: HTTP 500, empty body. An SSM-style typed `{ "error": … }` with 403 was expected.

findings.title: Service-token writes fail with RLS 42501 on the business-less canonical tables
findings.response: HTTP 200, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"isError":true,"content":[{"type":"text","text":"new row violates row-level security policy for table \"companies\""}]}}

findings.title: Three MCP write tools report success while writing nothing
findings.request: POST /api/v1/mcp tools/call nexus.add_note with lead_id = 00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000ff (valid UUID, no such lead)
findings.response: HTTP 200, result.structuredContent = {"note_id":null} with no isError flag. Same shape for create_task ({"task_id":null}) and submit_research ({"research_snapshot_id":null}).

findings.title: Idempotency metadata contradicts itself between the catalogue and the dispatch table
findings.request: POST /api/v1/mcp tools/call nexus.add_note with no idempotency_key (the handler table says this is unnecessary)
findings.response: HTTP 200, result.isError = true, text "idempotency_key is required for nexus.add_note" — i.e. the constant wins.

findings.title: nexus.finish_agent_run’s default state can never be inserted
findings.request: POST /api/v1/mcp tools/call nexus.finish_agent_run with { business_id, agent_name } and no state
findings.response: HTTP 200, result.isError = true, "new row for relation \"agent_runs\" violates check constraint \"agent_runs_state_check\"". Passing state:"succeeded" succeeds.

findings.title: nexus.submit_profile_capture is refused for a lead the caller can otherwise act on
findings.request: POST /api/v1/mcp tools/call nexus.submit_profile_capture with a real lead id, its LinkedIn URL and pasted content
findings.response: HTTP 200, result.isError = true, text "You do not have permission to do that."

findings.title: Three companion operations refuse the administrator with a blanket message
findings.request: POST /api/v1/companion/actions/mark-connection-sent { leadId: <real zemnas lead>, identityId: <real active identity>, withNote: true } as admin
findings.response: HTTP 400 {"error":"You do not have permission to do that."}

findings.title: nexus.get_today_queue answers a null/unknown user with an empty queue
The two scope vocabularies are disjoint, so the contract and the database disagree about a token’s authority
findings.code: packages/core/src/contracts.ts:535-554 (`MCP_TOOL_SCOPES`) and apps/web/src/app/api/v1/mcp/route.ts:675 (`handler.scope`) vs packages/db/migrations/0013_rls.sql (every `is_api_client_allowed(...)` call)
findings.request: A service token carrying only the contract scopes (`candidate:submit`, `signal:create`, …) then calling a write tool
findings.response: `42501 new row violates row-level security policy for table "signals"` (among others) even though the gateway’s scope check passed.

findings.title: Known dead code: `apps/web/middleware.ts` never executes
findings.response: 200/401 with `access-control-allow-origin: *` from the next.config.ts rule; a preflight returns 204 with the methods and headers advertised.
